prompt:
Normalise the one contact record embedded in the user's note. Return one bare JSON object with exactly the keys "name", "phone", "email", "company", "country", each a string or JSON null. No other text, fences, or keys.

### 1. Extract and route
Use only the block of contact label/value lines, which can have variant labels, arbitrary line order, and colon, equals, or tab separators. Ignore the surrounding note and signature. Trim values and collapse internal whitespace to one space. Treat absent or empty values and case-insensitive placeholders -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD as missing. Missing fields are null, with exactly one exception: the international-phone country lookup below.

A value containing @ is email. A value containing at least seven digits and otherwise only spaces or + - ( ) . / is phone, testing after removing leading tel: and a trailing extension (ext., ext, x, #, or extension followed by digits). Use content for these assignments even if the labels are swapped. Take explicit country only from the country line. Use the name and company labels unless the name-labelled value ends with a listed legal suffix and the company-labelled value does not; in that case swap those values before cleaning either.

### 2. Resolve phone and country together
Classify the phone after stripping tel: and the extension. Ignore an opening parenthesis when checking whether it begins with + or 00. If so, it is international: convert 00 to +, delete (0), and strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, and parentheses. Keep the written calling code.

Normalise an explicit country to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Recognise English, Swedish, and German names and alpha-2 or alpha-3 codes in any case. Recognise common aliases: UK and Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA and U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ. Explicit country wins even when it disagrees with the international phone; do not change that phone's calling code.

If the country line is absent, blank, or a placeholder and the phone is international, fill country from its calling code when the code belongs to exactly one country. For a shared code such as +1 or +7, leave country null. Do not infer country from anything else.

For a national phone, remove formatting punctuation and one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and the calling code of the normalised record country. Without a country, a national phone is null. Return every non-null phone in E.164: + and digits only.

### 3. Normalise the remaining fields
Name: split Last, First at the first comma and reorder to First Last. Drop leading honorifics Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof, ignoring case and optional dots. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate. String comparison is NFC-normalised.

Company: remove one trailing legal suffix, including an optional preceding comma, case-insensitively. Suffixes: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.

Email: remove a mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets; lowercase the whole address. Do not use an email domain or company suffix to supply any field. Do not guess or infer any value other than country from a unique international calling code as specified above.
